patient_overview.name: Velda Schuster
patient_overview.description: Velda Schuster is a 31-year-old Black, Hispanic woman from Union, New Jersey, currently pregnant and also managing prediabetes she's had since 2017, following a second-trimester miscarriage in 2023. She is warm, chatty, and clearly wants the student to like her, often answering a simple question with a ten-minute story that loops back around eventually. She has done real research online about gestational diabetes risk and prediabetes, and in the last few weeks has started genuinely trying to change how she eats, though the change feels new and shaky given how little daily support she has running a household of eight on a part-time income.

demographics.occupation: Part-time receptionist at a dental office
demographics.cultural_context: Velda grew up in Union, New Jersey, in a big extended family where meals were always stretched to feed whoever showed up, and she carries that same instinct now with her own household of eight. She identifies as Black and Hispanic and says food in her house was always "whatever filled the pot" rather than tied to one specific cuisine — rice, beans, chicken thighs, pasta, whatever was on sale. She values being the one people can lean on, which makes it hard for her to ask for help even when she's stretched thin herself.

medical_history: Past pregnancy history of miscarriage since 2019
Miscarriage in second trimester (2023-08 to 2023-09, resolved)
Complication occurring during pregnancy (2023-08 to 2023-09, resolved)
current_symptoms: Occasional lightheadedness in the late afternoon if she skips lunch
Fatigue most days, worse by evening after a full day of errands and kids
Occasional swelling in her feet by end of day
clinical_findings: Appears tired but animated, with dark circles under her eyes consistent with disrupted sleep in a full household
Mild ankle swelling noted when seated, legs often crossed/elevated for comfort
Skin and lips slightly dry; reports forgetting her water bottle most days
Speaks rapidly and gestures a lot, loses her thread mid-sentence then circles back to the original point

supplements_and_otc: Prenatal vitamin (take-home sample from her OB, takes most days)
Ginger chews she keeps in her purse for nausea

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Budget-driven mixed diet, heavy on starches and whatever stretches furthest for eight people; recently trying to add vegetables and protein at breakfast
food_preferences: Chicken thighs (whole packs, cheaper than breasts)
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Portion sizes at dinner when everyone eats together
Use of the Union food pantry near her church and what's actually available there
Juice and soda intake for the kids that she ends up finishing
Late-night snacking after everyone else is asleep
Skipping her own lunch to make sure the younger kids eat first
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Eats on the run most days; grabs toast or skips breakfast if rushed, bigger family dinner in the evening, sometimes nothing between
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly water now but still drinks sweet tea some afternoons; says she 'forgets' to drink water at work
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Walks to and from the bus stop and up three flights of stairs at home; no formal exercise, says she's 'always moving but never exercising'
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Ex-smoker (quit a few years ago); audit-c score of 1, drinks occasionally, maybe a glass of wine at a family gathering
nutrition_profile.sleep: Fragmented, 5-6 hours most nights, kids and household noise wake her, naps are rare

psychosocial_profile.personality: Warm, talkative, eager to be liked and seen as capable; brings humor into hard topics
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Tells long, winding stories that start on-topic and drift into family anecdotes before circling back; needs gentle redirecting but isn't offended by it
goals: Keep her blood sugar numbers good through the pregnancy
Model better eating for her kids without making a big deal of it
Lose the baby weight sensibly after delivery, not through a crash plan
concerns: That her prediabetes will turn into something worse after this baby
That she's not resting enough to keep her blood pressure down
That she won't be able to keep up the changes she just started once things get busy again
beliefs: She believes carbs 'in the right form' like oats and beans are fine, it's the sugary extras that hurt her
She believes her body let her down with the 2023 miscarriage and watches for any sign of trouble
She believes asking for help makes her look like she can't manage her own house
motivations: This pregnancy after the loss in 2023
Wanting energy to keep up with the other kids
Pride in being the one who holds the family together
fears: Losing this pregnancy the way she lost the one in 2023
Her prediabetes becoming diabetes and needing insulin
Not having anyone to call if something goes wrong at home
barriers: Very little day-to-day support with eight people in the household
Tight budget that limits fresh produce and lean protein
Part-time, inconsistent work hours that disrupt meal timing
Fatigue that undercuts her motivation some days
strengths: Reads up on gestational diabetes and prediabetes on her own and asks informed questions
Already started real changes in the last few weeks: oatmeal breakfasts, more water, smaller dinner portions
Resourceful with the food pantry and sales flyers
Social and well-connected, sees people often even if they aren't hands-on help
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Husband works long hours and is not very hands-on with meals or appointments; older kids help some with younger siblings but it's inconsistent; sees friends often socially but has almost no one she can call for practical day-to-day help
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Action stage but fragile - started real changes a few weeks ago and is proud of them, but admits one bad week could undo it

initial_information: She's pregnant and has had prediabetes since 2017
She lost a pregnancy in 2023 in the second trimester and is nervous about this one
She's started eating oatmeal and drinking more water the last few weeks
She has eight people in her household and does most of the cooking
discoverable_information: She shops with sales flyers and sometimes uses the food pantry near her church
Her husband works long hours and isn't involved in meal planning
She skips her own lunch some days so the younger kids eat first
She reads a lot about gestational diabetes and prediabetes online
Her sleep is broken most nights because of the kids and the house noise
reluctant_information: She admits, when asked gently about her prenatal vitamin, that she sometimes 'forgets' it for a few days in a row because it makes her nauseous on an empty stomach
She hesitates before saying she doesn't always take it with food the way the clinic told her to, which is why it bothers her stomach
hidden_information: Velda has not told anyone, including her OB, that she stopped taking her prenatal vitamin for an entire week in August 2026 because the nausea got bad and she was scared to mention it in case they'd lecture her
She worries privately that her weight gain since 2023 means she somehow caused the miscarriage, though she's never said this out loud to a provider
